title: The Passion of Saint John the Baptist
short_summary: This memorial recalls the martyrdom of Saint John the Baptist, beheaded by Herod for his fearless proclamation of the truth about marriage.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar keeps this memorial on August 29.
The Gospels of Mark and Matthew recount John's imprisonment and execution by Herod Antipas.
John was killed for publicly condemning Herod's unlawful marriage to Herodias.
His death is recalled distinctly from his birth, celebrated as a solemnity on June 24.

sections.heading: Imprisoned for speaking the truth
sections.body: The Gospels recount that John the Baptist was imprisoned by Herod Antipas after publicly condemning Herod's marriage to Herodias, his brother's wife, as unlawful. John's willingness to confront a ruler at personal cost follows directly from his prophetic mission to prepare the way of the Lord.

sections.heading: Beheaded at a birthday feast
sections.body: According to the Gospel accounts, Herodias's daughter danced before Herod at a banquet and, prompted by her mother, asked for John's head on a platter. Herod, bound by a rash oath made before his guests, had John beheaded in prison.

sections.heading: The Forerunner's final witness
sections.body: John's death completes his mission as the Forerunner: having prepared the way for Christ in his preaching, he goes before the Lord even in the manner of his death, a martyr for the truth about marriage and moral conduct before Christ's own Passion.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Truth spoken to power
catholic_connection_sections.body: John's martyrdom shows that prophetic witness to moral truth, even about matters as personal as marriage, can demand the highest cost. His death stands as an early Christian instance of martyrdom for the truth of the moral law, not only for confessing Christ's name directly.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Red for a martyr's witness
catholic_connection_sections.body: Red marks this memorial as a martyr's feast. Even as the Baptist's own birth and mission point entirely to Christ, his death likewise anticipates the Passion of the Lord he came to announce.
